messages:
incident-bot: Pager triggered — WUS6 serving group: elevated kv-cache eviction and 5xx rate increase detected across zone-c. Severity: P1. Auto-escalation to oncall. Links: https://alerts.redwood.internal/2532467890, runbook: #runbooks/kv-cache-pressure

simon_oncall: On it. Paging in. Looking at metrics now. Oncall handoff: simon -> maria if this needs kernel patching.

maria_sre: I see a KV cache pressure spike at 13:04 UTC, eviction rate spiked from 0.2% -> 12% and tail latency for short seqs jumped ~120ms. Errors are concentrated on instances in zone-c. Query pattern looks like a mix of batched small requests plus a few runaway prefixes.

alex_eng: tagging infra: could be a bad leader in the sharded in-memory layer. I'll check leader election logs and `kvstore` OOMs.

jess_ops: Running quick mitigation: increasing local cache size on the pool and lowering batch window to reduce KV churn. Applying temporary route-diversion to west-us2 and east-us1 for non-pin customers. ETA for routing change ~5m.

jess_ops: command I'm running (attachment):
```
# divert 40% of traffic from wus6-zone-c to wus2
redwood route update --from=region:wus6:zone:c --split=40 --to=region:wus2
# apply reduced batch window
redwood config set serving.batch_window_ms=8 --pool=wus6-zone-c
```

nate_support: Heads up: customers with pinned Dedicated pools won't be rerouted. I'll compile a short list of impacted tenants and their owners now.

emma_prod: Preparing a status page blurb. Draft below — feedback pls: "We're investigating increased error rates and latency for inference in the west-us6 (zone-c) region. Some requests are being rerouted to adjacent regions while we mitigate. Customers with pinned deployments are not affected by reroutes; we'll provide ETA updates shortly."

maria_sre: Quick health snapshot:
- kv_eviction_rate: zone-c hosts 3/6 above threshold
- cpu/mem: normal on most hosts
- disk: unaffected
- gc/oom: no full OOMs, but GC pauses slightly elevated on 2 nodes
I recommend: 1) immediate 30-40% reroute for best-effort traffic, 2) restart leader on host zid-cc-07 after draining, 3) increase pool replicas if pressure persists.

chris_network: Network topo looks fine, no cross-AZ peering flaps. Egress bandwidth not saturated. Reroute should be safe.

alex_eng: Found repeated `leader-lease` renew failures on zid-cc-07 and zid-cc-09 around 13:02 UTC. Suspect flaky NVMe on one host causing tail latency and KV eviction thrash. I'll take zid-cc-07 out of rotation for maintenance.

simon_oncall: Handoff note for second-shift: I will stay on for 30m while we verify the reroute effects and carry out restarts. If eviction rate doesn't drop inside 20 minutes, escalate to infra-eng and consider scaling the model pool by +1 replica.

jess_ops: Reroute applied: 40% traffic -> wus2, 20% -> eus1 for best-effort. Observability: token-level cost bucket shows immediate drop in error rate on diverted traffic, region error-rate for wus6 down from 8.9% -> 4.1% in the last 3 minutes.

incident-bot: Update: Pager suppressed due to active mitigation (rule: auto-silence on successful reroute). Next automated check in 5m.

nate_support: Customer-impact summary draft for CS/Account teams: "We experienced elevated error rates and latency impacting inference traffic in west-us6 zone-c starting at ~13:02 UTC. For non-pinned workloads we diverted a portion of traffic to adjacent regions; effects reduced customer-facing errors. Dedicated/pinned customers unaffected by reroute. We're performing host restarts and additional replica scaling as needed. We'll update within 30 minutes." Thoughts?

emma_prod: Suggest adding an ETA window: "Next update by 13:45 UTC." Also include contact for mitigation: support@redwood.ai and your account manager.

maria_sre: I'm capturing the commands used and will add to postmortem. Quick note on rollback: if reroute causes unexpected downstream cold-start regressions, we can reduce split percent back in increments of 10% via `redwood route update` CLI.

alex_eng: Zid-cc-07 taken OOS, performing controlled restart of serving process. Replicas +1 scheduled for the pool; autoscaler check running.

jess_ops: Monitoring tail latency dashboards — good sign: p99 token latency for routed traffic is stable in wus2 & eus1. Overall p95 for the product route improved ~70ms.

chris_network: Verified no network ACL changes required. BGP sessions steady across peering.

simon_oncall: After 18 minutes post-reroute: eviction_rate down to 1.3% cluster-wide, 1.8% in zone-c. Error rate falling. Keeping page open for one more verification loop then we'll transition to incident notes + postmortem.

nate_support: Sending customer-facing notification now (CS template used):
```
Hi <Customer>,
We observed an intermittent increase in errors and latency for inference requests in west-us6 zone-c at ~13:02 UTC. We routed a portion of traffic to adjacent regions to restore service for non-pinned workloads. Your dedicated deployments were not rerouted and were not affected. Our engineers are performing host-level restarts and will follow up with a full incident report. Next update by 13:45 UTC.
Regards, Redwood Support
```

emma_prod: Posting to status page: "Degraded performance in west-us6 (zone-c). Mitigation in progress — partial traffic reroutes to adjacent regions. Some requests may experience higher latency or transient errors."

maria_sre: Adding checklist for post-incident: impact window, root cause hypothesis (flaky NVMe + leader renew failure), mitigation timeline, telemetry exports, customer list, and follow-up actions (replace host, tighten leader lease renew retries).

simon_oncall: OK handing off now to maria for follow-up and postmortem. If anything spikes again, page oncall with severity P1.

maria_sre: Acknowledged. I'll produce a short incident summary and coordinate the postmortem draft. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident resolved->monitoring state changed to "stabilizing". Final note will be published after postmortem is filed.
